(p-5828) In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.
Surah At-Talaq (The Divorce)

Al-Mahayimi said: It is named so because it explains the manner of the lawful (sunnah) divorce and what follows from divorce of the waiting period (iddah), maintenance (nafaqah), and residence (sukna).

It is also called "The Lesser Surah of Women" (Surat an-Nisa' al-Qusra). It is Medinan, and its verses number twelve.

(p-5829) In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.
The discussion on the interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words:

[1] ﴿O Prophet, when you divorce women, divorce them at their prescribed time, and count the waiting period. And fear Allah, your Lord. Do not expel them from their houses, nor should they leave, unless they commit a clear immorality. These are the limits of Allah, and whoever transgresses the limits of Allah has certainly wronged himself. You do not know; perhaps Allah will bring about after that some matter.﴾

﴿O Prophet, when you divorce women, divorce them at their prescribed time﴾ meaning: at their appointed time, which is the state of purity (tuhr). So the "lam" here indicates a specification of time.

An-Nasir said: The "iddah" was made the time-frame for the divorce commanded, even though it is originally a verbal noun (masdar). The Arabs often use verbal nouns as adverbs of time, like "khufuq an-najm" (the setting of the star) and "maqdim al-hajj" (the arrival of the pilgrims). Since the iddah is the time-frame for the commanded divorce, and its time is the state of purity, then the purity has a waiting period.

Ibn Jarir said: That is, when you divorce your wives, divorce them in their state of purity during which they count their waiting period, being pure without having had intercourse. And do not divorce them during their menstruation, the period which does not count for them from their "quru'" (periods).

Then it was narrated from Qatadah, who said: The "iddah" is that he divorces her while she is pure without intercourse, with a single pronouncement.

Ibn Kathir said: From this, the jurists derived the rulings of divorce and divided it into: the divorce of the sunnah (talaq as-sunnah), and the divorce of innovation (talaq al-bid'ah). The divorce of the sunnah is that he divorces her while she is pure without having had intercourse with her, or while she is pregnant and her pregnancy has become evident. The innovated divorce is that he divorces her during menstruation, or during a purity in which he has had intercourse with her, and he does not know whether she has conceived or not. And there is a third divorce that has neither sunnah nor bid'ah, which is the divorce of a minor girl, a woman past menopause, and a woman who has not been consummated with. There will come in the notes further elaboration on this.

(p-5830) ﴿And count the waiting period﴾ meaning: keep track of it, and complete it as three periods (qur'). ﴿And fear Allah, your Lord. Do not expel them from their houses﴾ meaning: fear Him by not transgressing His limits concerning divorced women. So do not expel them from the houses in which you had lodged them before the divorce, out of anger toward them and dislike of living with them, because they have the right to residence until their waiting period ends.

﴿Nor should they leave﴾ meaning: by their own independent decision, of their own accord.

An-Nasir said: His, the Exalted's, words ﴿And fear Allah, your Lord﴾ are a preparation for His words ﴿Do not expel them from their houses﴾, as if He forbade expulsion twice: once as included in the general prohibition, and once singled out specifically. Similar examples have already passed.

﴿Unless they commit a clear immorality﴾ meaning: then they may leave. "Al-fahisha" (immorality) is adultery; or that the divorced woman acts abusively toward her family; or it is every ugly act in which its limit is transgressed, so that it includes adultery, theft, and abuse of the in-laws and the like. The last is the view preferred by Ibn Jarir, adhering to the general wording of the noble text.

﴿These are the limits of Allah, and whoever transgresses the limits of Allah has certainly wronged himself﴾ meaning: by exposing himself to punishment through the sin he has earned. Or he harms himself by what he acquires of intense aversion and severe hatred, which may intensify so that reconciliation becomes difficult, whereas the better course is to lessen animosity and remedy estrangement. This is the more apparent meaning; therefore He, glorified be He, said:

﴿You do not know; perhaps Allah will bring about after that some matter﴾, for it is a resumptive statement (isti'naf) given to explain the content of the conditional clause.

Abu as-Su'ud said: They have said that the matter which Allah brings about is that He turns his heart from what he did by transgression to its opposite. Therefore the wronging must be an expression of a worldly harm that befalls him because of his transgression, and cannot be remedied, or of general harm encompassing both worldly and otherworldly harm. The explanation is restricted to the worldly harm because people's caution against it is greater and their concern to avert it is stronger.

His, the Exalted's, words ﴿You do not know﴾ are an address to the transgressor by way of iltifat (a shift in grammatical person), for the sake of greater emphasis on restraining from transgression, not to the Prophet (ﷺ), as has been mistakenly assumed. The meaning is: whoever transgresses the limits of Allah has harmed himself; for you, (p-5831) O transgressor, do not know the outcome of the matter. Perhaps Allah will bring about in your heart, after what you did of transgression, a matter which requires the opposite of what you did, so that He changes your hatred into love, and your turning away into turning toward her, and it becomes possible to remedy it by return (raj'ah) or by a new marriage contract. End.

Notes:

First: In "al-Iklil," it says: "The Prophet (ﷺ) explained His words ﴿for their waiting period﴾ as: that she be divorced in a purity in which he has not had intercourse with her." Related by al-Bukhari and Muslim. In Muslim's wording, he recited: "divorce them at the beginning of their waiting period." The jurists used this as evidence that the sunnah divorce is what has been mentioned, and that divorce during menstruation, or during a purity in which intercourse occurred, is an innovated and prohibited divorce. Some people used the verse as evidence that it does not take effect during menstruation.

Second: In "al-Iklil," regarding His words ﴿Do not expel them from their houses﴾: there is an obligation of residence for her as long as she is in the waiting period, and it is forbidden to expel her or for her to leave, ﴿unless they commit a clear immorality﴾, such as bad character and abusing her in-laws. Then she may move out.

Third: In "al-Iklil," he used His words ﴿You do not know; perhaps Allah will bring about after that some matter﴾ as evidence by those who do not require residence except in a revocable divorce. Ibn Abi Hatim related from al-Hasan and Ikrimah that he said: The woman divorced three times, and the widow, have no residence and no maintenance, because of His words: ﴿perhaps Allah will bring about after that some matter﴾, and what happens after the three [pronouncements] is not possible.

Fourth: As some of the wise have said: When harmony between the spouses has become impossible, and there is no longer any possibility of reconciliation, and the husband insists on it, because the presence of two people of conflicting temperaments who hate each other, such that neither looks at the other without feeling aversion in his soul and enmity in his heart, each striving to harm the other, is an evil and corruption that must be eliminated and cut off. End.

Ibn al-Qayyim said in "I'lam al-Lahfan" (Ighathat al-Lahfan): Since Allah, glorified and exalted be He, hates divorce, because it breaks the wife and agrees with the pleasure of His enemy Iblis, who rejoices at the separation from obedience to Allah through marriage, which is obligatory or recommended, and because it exposes each spouse to immorality and disobedience, and other corruptions of divorce; yet the husband or the wife may need it, and there is benefit in it when it is legislated in a manner that brings about benefit and averts harm. He forbade it in other than that manner. So He legislated it in the best manner and the closest to the interest of the husband and the wife. He legislated that he divorce her while she is pure without intercourse, with a single pronouncement, and then leave her until her waiting period ends. If the evil between them is removed and agreement is reached, he has a way to mend the rift and return the marital bed as it was. Otherwise, he leaves her until her waiting period has ended. If his desire follows her, he has a way to propose to her and renew the contract with her consent. And if his desire does not follow her, he leaves her, and she marries whomever she wishes.

He made the waiting period three periods so that the period of respite and choice would be prolonged. This is what He legislated and permitted. He did not permit the final separation after consummation except by mutual consent through annulment or ransom (ifida'). So if he divorces her once after another, one pronouncement remains for him. If he divorces her a third time, He forbids her to him as a punishment, and it is not lawful for him to marry her again until she marries another husband, and he consummates the marriage with her, and then she is separated from him by death or divorce. If he knows that his beloved will go to someone else and enjoy him instead of him, he refrains from divorce. End.

The topics of divorce and its branches deserve to be studied in "I'lam al-Lahfan" and "Zad al-Ma'ad" by Ibn al-Qayyim, and "Fatawa Ibn Taymiyyah" by his teacher. Whoever has not examined what the two of them verified and strove to make clear has missed abundant knowledge and a luminous criterion. And success is from Allah.

(p-5833) Fifth: Those who say that pronouncing the divorce all at once is not legislated have used these verses as evidence. The Imam Ibn al-Qayyim said in "I'lam al-Lahfan": The argument from the verse is from several aspects:

The first: He, the Exalted, legislated only that she be divorced for her waiting period, meaning for the commencement of her waiting period, so he divorces with a divorce that is followed by her beginning the waiting period. For this reason, "the Prophet (peace be upon him) commanded 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with both of them, when he divorced his wife, that he should take her back, and he recited this verse as an explanation of what it means." The meaning is divorce at the beginning of the waiting period. 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar also used to recite it this way. For this reason, everyone who holds that it is forbidden to combine three pronouncements has said: It is not permissible for him to follow the first divorce with another in that same purity, because he is not divorcing for the waiting period. The waiting period has begun from the time of the first divorce, so the second is not for the waiting period and is not authorized, since the waiting period is counted from the first divorce, because it is a divorce for the waiting period, unlike the second and third. Whoever holds it to be legislated says: it is the divorce at the completion of the waiting period, and divorce at its completion is like divorce at its beginning, and both are divorce for the waiting period. The proponents of the first view say: the meaning of divorce for the waiting period is divorce at its beginning, as in the other reading which explains the well-known reading: "divorce them at the beginning of their waiting period." They said: If it is not legislated to follow one divorce with another before revocation or a contract, then combining them together is even less legitimate and more unlikely. Following one divorce with another is easier than combining them, and for this reason those who do not permit combining in one purity have legislated following in separate purities.

Ibn 'Abbas argued for the prohibition of combining three pronouncements by this verse. Mujahid said: I was with Ibn 'Abbas when a man came and said: "He divorced his wife three times." He remained silent until I thought he would take her back. Then he said: "One of you goes and rides the foolishness, then says: 'O Ibn 'Abbas!' Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Whoever fears Allah, He will make for him a way out﴾ [At-Talaq: 2], and I find no way out for you. You have disobeyed your Lord, and your wife has become separated from you. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿O Prophet, when you divorce women, divorce them﴾ at the beginning of their waiting period." This is a sound report. Ibn 'Abbas understood from the verse that combining three pronouncements is forbidden, and this is the understanding of the one for whom the Prophet (ﷺ) prayed that he be given understanding of the religion and taught the interpretation, and it is among the best understandings, as has been established.

(p-5834) The second aspect of the argument from the verse is His words: ﴿Do not expel them from their houses, nor should they leave﴾. This applies only to the revocable divorce. As for the irrevocable divorce, she has no residence and no maintenance, because of the sound sunnah of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), whose authenticity cannot be challenged and whose clear meaning contains no doubt. This shows that this is the ruling for every divorce that Allah has legislated, as long as it was not preceded by two pronouncements before it. For this reason, the majority said: it is not legislated for him, and he does not have the right to make her irrevocably separated with a single pronouncement without compensation. Abu Hanifah said: he has the right to do that, because revocation is his right, and he has waived it. The majority say: although revocation is a right for him, she has marital rights over him, so he does not have the right to waive them except by a khul' (divorce for compensation), or by completing the number, as the Qur'an indicates.

The third aspect: He said: ﴿And these are the limits of Allah, and whoever transgresses the limits of Allah has certainly wronged himself﴾. So if he divorces her three times at once, he has transgressed the limits of Allah, and thus he is a wrongdoer.

The fourth aspect: He, glorified be He, said: ﴿You do not know; perhaps Allah will bring about after that some matter﴾. The most knowledgeable of the Ummah in the Qur'an, namely the Companions, understood that the "matter" here is revocation. They said: "And what matter could come about after three?"

The fifth aspect: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then when they have reached their term, either retain them in good manner or part from them in good manner﴾ [al-Talaq: 2]. This is the ruling for every divorce that He legislated, except when it is preceded by two pronouncements before it. Ibn 'Abbas argued for the prohibition of combining three (talaq) with His saying, exalted is He: "O Prophet, when you divorce women, divorce them at the commencement of their waiting period," as has preceded. This is true, for the verse, if it indicates the prohibition of following one divorce with another in one purity or in several purities, before a return (raj'ah) or a contract (aqd), as has preceded, because he would then be divorcing at other than the commencement of the waiting period, then it is even more fitting and more apt that it indicates the prohibition of combining.

They said: God, glory be to Him, legislated divorce in the easiest and most gentle manner for the husband and the wife, so that the servant does not hasten to pronounce it and to part from his beloved. He also set a term for the waiting period so that his words may be retracted by return (raj'ah). (p-5835) Thus He did not permit him to divorce the woman during her menstruation, because that is the time of his aversion from her and his inability to enjoy her, nor immediately after intercourse with her, because he has then fulfilled his purpose from her, and perhaps his desire for her has waned, and he is indifferent to keeping her since he has satisfied his need. If he divorces her in these two states, he may perhaps regret it afterwards, in addition to the prolongation of the waiting period it entails, and [divorcing her] immediately after intercourse with her husband, since her womb may have conceived a child from him, so he would not want to separate from her. As for when she has menstruated and then become pure, his soul yearns for her, due to the long time since his intercourse with her, so he does not proceed to divorce her in this state except out of need for it. The Lawgiver therefore did not permit him to divorce her except in this state, or in a state where her pregnancy has become evident, because his proceeding to divorce her in this state too is evidence of his need for divorce. The Prophet ﷺ confirmed this by forbidding 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar to divorce in the purity that follows the menstruation in which he had divorced her; rather, he ordered him to take her back until she becomes pure, then menstruates, then becomes pure again, and if it then seems right to him to divorce her, he may divorce her. In this there are several wisdoms:

Among them: the purity directly connected to the menstruation is, together with it, the ruling of a single qur' (period), so if he divorces her in that purity, it is as if he divorced her during the menstruation, because it is connected to it and joined with it, like one thing.

The second: if he were permitted to divorce her in that purity, he would be taking her back for the sake of divorce, and this is the opposite of the purpose of return (raj'ah), for God, exalted is He, legislated it only for retention, for the benefit of marriage and the restoration of the marital bed. So it should not be for the sake of divorce, otherwise it would be as if he had taken her back in order to divorce her. Return was legislated only so that he may retain her. On this very basis we have invalidated the marriage of the muhallil (the one who makes lawful by a marriage of intermediary), for God, glory and exalted is He, legislated marriage for retention and companionship, whereas the muhallil marries in order to divorce, so he opposes God in His legislation and His religion.

The third: if he is patient with her until she menstruates, then becomes pure, then menstruates and becomes pure again, the anger in his soul that drives him to divorce dissipates, and perhaps the situation between them improves and what calls him to divorce ceases, so the prolonging of this period is a mercy to him and to her. Since the Lawgiver takes into account such mercy and compassion towards the husband, and legislated divorce in this manner, which is the furthest thing from regret, how is it fitting (p-5836) for His legislation to prescribe the irrevocable separation of her and her prohibition to him by a single word that combines what He legislated separately, such that he has no way back to her? And how can the wisdom of the Lawgiver and the wisdom of this (practice) coincide? These aspects and the like of them, by which the majority (al-jumhur) demonstrated that combining three (divorces) is not legislated, are themselves what determine that it does not take effect, and that only what is legislated takes effect alone, namely the single (pronouncement).

The commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 65, verse 2:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[2] ﴿So when they have reached their term, either retain them in kindness or part from them in kindness, and call to witness two just men from among you, and establish the testimony for Allah. This is what is admonished to whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day. And whoever fears Allah – He will make for him a way out.﴾

﴿When they have reached their term﴾ means: the divorced women who are in their waiting period (*'iddah*, the prescribed waiting period). ﴿Their term﴾ means the end of the waiting period, that is, when its completion is near and they are about to reach it. ﴿Then retain them in kindness﴾ means: take them back in accordance with what Allah has commanded you regarding the rights He has made obligatory for them, of maintenance, clothing, housing, and good companionship. ﴿Or part from them in kindness﴾ means: leave them until their waiting periods end, so that they become separated from you (*yabinna*) in kindness, which is to give them what is due to them of right, such as the dowry and the consolation gift (*mut'ah*), as he is obligated to give them.

﴿And call to witness two just men from among you﴾ means: call to witness, at the time of the taking back (*raj'ah*) and at the time of separation, persons whose religion and trustworthiness are acceptable.

Ibn 'Abbas said: If he takes her back, she is his on the basis of two pronouncements of divorce. If he does not take her back, and her waiting period ends, then she has become separated from him by one divorce, and she has the right to dispose of herself, so she may marry whomever she wishes, him or another.

This calling of witnesses to the taking back and to the divorce is recommended (*mandub*). Some scholars held that it is obligatory for both. Others distinguished between the taking back, which they made obligatory, and the separation, which they considered recommended. The apparent meaning of the command in the verse is obligation in both cases, and preference (*tarjih*) must rest on a preponderating proof. What supports the obligation is that the commands throughout the verse, before and after it, are by consensus (*ijma'*) for obligation, and there is no proof that diverts the command to call witnesses from its apparent meaning. So it remains like what precedes and follows it. Although the Qur'an does not establish that a ruling is shared by parallel cases, it is a supporting and confirming consideration when no diverting factor exists.

Furthermore, the command to call witnesses at divorce indicates that swearing an oath of divorce, or making its occurrence conditional upon some matter, is not considered divorce in the Shari'ah. This is because whatever requires witnesses must involve a person intending to effect it, resolving upon it, and preparing for it. It is fitting that when one intends to dissolve a marital bond, which is a contract of the strongest covenant, one should call witnesses to it, after it has been preceded by a process of arbitration by two arbiters from the side of the spouses, as the verse of arbitration (*ayat al-hukm*) indicates. So let the lawful divorce and the innovated divorce be carefully considered. And success is from Allah.

Al-Zamakhshari said: It has been said that the benefit of calling witnesses is that there should be no denial between them, that he not be accused of retaining her, and that, should one of them die, the surviving one not claim that the marriage still existed in order to inherit.

﴿And establish the testimony for Allah﴾ means: for His sake alone, sincerely. That is, they should establish it not for the sake of the one in whose favour it is given, nor against the one against whom it is given, nor for any other purpose, apart from upholding the truth and repelling injustice, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Be steadfast in upholding justice, witnesses for Allah, even if it be against yourselves﴾ [al-Nisa': 135]. End of quotation.

The verse indicates the prohibition of taking payment for giving testimony. This is supported by His saying: ﴿This is what is admonished to whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day﴾, for what is referred to is the urging to establish testimony for the sake of Allah and for the purpose of upholding justice. It is also possible that the reference ("this") returns to everything mentioned in the verse.

﴿And whoever fears Allah – He will make for him a way out.﴾

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[3] ﴿And He will provide for him from where he does not expect. And whoever relies upon Allah, then He is sufficient for him. Indeed, Allah will accomplish His purpose. Allah has already set for everything a destiny.﴾

﴿And He will provide for him from where he does not expect﴾. Al-Zamakhshari said: It is permissible that this be a parenthetical clause (jumlah i'tiradiyyah) emphasizing what preceded concerning carrying out the divorce according to the Sunnah and its best and most distant-from-regret manner.

And the meaning is: whoever fears Allah and divorces according to the Sunnah, not harming the woman in waiting (al-mu'taddah), not expelling her from her dwelling, taking precaution and calling witnesses, Allah will make for him a way out of the distresses and the entanglements that come with marital matters, will relieve him of them, grant him ease, and give him deliverance, and will provide for him from a direction he does not imagine or reckon, if he pays the dowry, fulfills the rights and maintenance, even if his wealth is little. It is also permissible that it be brought in as a digression (istitrad) at the mention of His words: ﴿That is what you are admonished with﴾ [al-Talaq: 2], meaning: whoever fears Allah, He will make for him a way out and a deliverance from the distresses of this world and the Hereafter. End of quotation.

Note (tanbih):

Ibn al-Faras said: Most of the exegetes said: the meaning of the verse concerning divorce is, namely: whoever does not exceed the divorce of the Sunnah to the divorce of three will have Allah make for him a way out if he regrets it in the revocation (raj'ah). He said: This is used as evidence for the prohibition of combining three divorces, and that if they are combined they take effect. Transmitted by him in "al-Iklil".

Ibn al-Qayyim said in "al-Ighathah": Know that whoever fears Allah regarding his divorce, and divorces as Allah and His Messenger commanded and legislated for him, Allah will suffice him from all stratagems. For this reason, after mentioning the ruling of legislated divorce, Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him a way out﴾ [al-Talaq: 2]. If most of those who divorce feared Allah, they would be free through their piety from burdens, shackles, deceit and scheming. The divorce that Allah, glorified is He, legislated is that one divorces her while she is in a state of purity without having had intercourse, divorces her once, then leaves her until her waiting period ends. If it becomes apparent to him that he should retain her during the waiting period, he retains her. If he does not return to her until her waiting period has ended, he may enter a new contract with her without another husband. If he has no purpose, it does not harm him for her to marry another man. Whoever does this does not regret, and does not need a stratagem or a halala (legal marriage to restore the wife). For this reason Ibn 'Abbas was asked about a man who divorced his wife a hundred times, and he said: You have disobeyed your Lord, and you have separated from your wife; you did not fear Allah, so He would not make for you a way out.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: A man came to Ibn 'Abbas and said: "I divorced my wife a thousand times." He said: "As for three, your wife becomes unlawful to you, and the rest are a burden of sin. You have taken the signs of Allah in mockery."

Mujahid said: I was with Ibn 'Abbas when a man came to him and said: "He divorced his wife three times." So he fell silent until I thought he would return her to him. Then he said: "One of you goes and rides the foolishness, then says: O Ibn 'Abbas! And Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him a way out﴾ [al-Talaq: 2]. But you have not feared Allah, so I find no way out for you. You have disobeyed your Lord, and your wife has become separated from you." Related by Abu Dawud. The discussion is lengthy in its ramifications and one cannot do without consulting it.

﴿And whoever relies upon Allah, then He is sufficient for him﴾: that is, whoever relies upon what He legislated, and entrusts his affair to what He made the way out, for there is no more effective remedy than that. ﴿Indeed, Allah will accomplish His purpose﴾: it was read with the genitive (idafah), meaning: He attains what He wills of His affair. So whoever is certain entrusts his affair to Him and relies upon Him. It was also read: ﴿Indeed, Allah will accomplish His purpose﴾, meaning: complete and perfect is His affair, His judgment and His legislation, because of the wisdoms and mercy within it. ﴿Allah has already set for everything a destiny﴾: that is, a limit and a measure, as wisdom requires. Among this is His measuring what was measured in the matter of divorce, through what He explained concerning its regulation and timing, the knowledge of the way out from it.

The discussion concerning His saying, exalted is He:

[4] ﴿And those of your women who have despaired of menstruation, if you have doubt, their waiting period is three months, and [the same for] those who have not menstruated. And for those who are pregnant, their term is until they deliver their burden. And whoever fears Allah – He will make for him of his affair ease.﴾

﴿And those of your women who have despaired of menstruation, if you have doubt﴾ means: their ruling has become unclear to you, or you are in doubt about the blood that appears from them due to their old age – is it from menstruation or is it from istihadah (irregular bleeding)? ﴿Their waiting period is three months, and [the same for] those who have not menstruated﴾ means: of the young girls, due to their youth, when their husbands divorce them after consummation, their waiting period is three months. The predicate has been omitted because of what is indicated by what was mentioned. ﴿And for those who are pregnant, their term﴾ (p-5840) is in the completion of their waiting periods ﴿is until they deliver their burden﴾ means: what is in their wombs. The verse is general concerning divorced women and women whose husbands have died.

It is related from ʿAlī and Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, that the verse is specific to divorced women. As for the widow, her waiting period is the later of the two terms.

Ibn Jarir said: The correct view is that it is general concerning all pregnant women, because Allah, exalted is He, stated the matter in a general way and did not specify the report concerning a divorced woman to the exclusion of a widow.

If it is said: The context of the report concerns the rulings on divorced women. It is answered: Its wording is an independent statement about the rulings on the number of waiting periods for all pregnant women, divorced and non-divorced.

In the two Sahihs (of al-Bukhari and Muslim): "From Umm Salamah that Subay'ah al-Aslamiyyah gave birth forty nights after the death of her husband, and then she was proposed to, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ permitted her to marry," and Abu al-Sanabil was among those who proposed to her.

﴿And whoever fears Allah﴾ means: he does not oppose His command regarding the divorce of his wife. ﴿He will make for him of his affair ease﴾ means: facilitating the taking back (of the wife) as long as she is within her waiting period, and the ability to propose to her if it has ended and she has been called to him by reason of piety.

"The statement concerning the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[5] ﴿That is the command of Allah, which He has sent down to you. And whoever fears Allah, He will remove from him his misdeeds and enlarge for him his reward.﴾

﴿That﴾ means: what has been mentioned of the rulings on divorce, return (al-raj'ah), and the waiting period (al-'iddah). ﴿is the command of Allah, which He has sent down to you﴾ (p-5841) means: so that you may comply with it and act upon it. ﴿And whoever fears Allah, He will remove from him his misdeeds and enlarge for him his reward﴾ means: by multiplication."

**Commentary on the interpretation of His words, may He be exalted:**

[6] ﴿Let them dwell where you dwell, according to your means, and do not harm them so as to constrain them. And if they are pregnant, then spend on them until they give birth. Then if they nurse for you, give them their payment, and confer among yourselves in kindness. But if you disagree, then another woman will nurse for him.﴾

﴿Let them dwell where you dwell according to your means﴾: that is, according to your wealth which you have, your capacity and your ability. ﴿And do not harm them﴾: that is, do not treat them with harm. ﴿So as to constrain them﴾: that is, in the dwelling, by some means, such as bringing in someone who is not agreeable to them, or occupying their space, or other such things, until you force them to leave or to ransom themselves.

**Note:**

In *al-Iklil* he said: The verse indicates the obligation of residence (*sukna*) for all divorced women, and for the irrevocably divorced (*al-bawa'in*, women whose divorce is final), because of the precedence of residence for the revocably divorced (*al-raj'iyyat*, women who may be taken back), and because of His words after it: ﴿And if they are pregnant, then spend on them﴾, for that is specific to the irrevocably divorced. It also indicates that provision of residence is judged by the condition of the husband, and the prohibition of harming them through it, and forcing them to leave.

﴿And if they are pregnant, then spend on them until they give birth﴾: Ibn Jarir said: that is, and if your divorced wives are pregnant and have been irrevocably divorced by you, then spend on them during their waiting period (*'idda*) from you until they give birth.

On the authority of Ibn 'Abbas regarding the verse, he said: This is a woman whose husband divorces her, finalizing the divorce while she is pregnant. Allah commands him to provide her residence and spend on her until she gives birth. And if she nurses, then until she weans. And if he divorces her finally while she is not pregnant, then she has the right to residence until her waiting period ends, and there is no maintenance. Likewise a woman whose husband dies leaving her: if she is pregnant, he spends on her from the share of her unborn child if there is an inheritance; and if there is no inheritance, the heir spends on her until she gives birth and weans her child, as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And upon the heir is the like of that﴾ [al-Baqarah: 233]. If she is not pregnant, her maintenance is from her own property.

Then Ibn Jarir said: Others said that by His words ﴿And if they are pregnant, then spend on them until they give birth﴾ He meant every divorced woman, whether her husband has the right of return or not, and among those who said this were 'Umar ibn al-Khattab and 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with them both.

On the authority of Ibrahim, he said: 'Umar and 'Abdullah would give the divorced woman three things: residence, maintenance and consolation payment (*al-mut'a*). And when the hadith of Fatima bint Qays was mentioned to 'Umar, that the Prophet (ﷺ) «commanded her to observe her waiting period outside her husband's house», he said: "We would not permit the testimony of a woman in our religion."

Then Ibn Jarir said: The correct view in this matter, in our opinion, is that there is no maintenance for the irrevocably divorced woman except if she is pregnant. This is because Allah, may His praise be exalted, made maintenance, by His words ﴿And if they are pregnant, then spend on them﴾, only for pregnant women, to the exclusion of other irrevocably divorced women from their husbands. Had the irrevocably divorced pregnant and non-pregnant women been equal in the obligation of maintenance from their husbands, there would be no understandable reason for singling out pregnant women in the mention in this place, since they and others are equal in that. In singling them out without others is the clearest evidence that there is no maintenance for the irrevocably divorced except if she is pregnant. And by what we have said, the report from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is authentically established.

«Abu Salama ibn 'Abd al-Rahman said: Fatima bint Qays, sister of al-Dahhak ibn Qays, narrated to me: (p-5843) that Abu 'Amr al-Makhzumi divorced her three times, and he ordered that she be given maintenance, but she considered it insufficient. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had sent him to Yemen. So Khalid ibn al-Walid set out with a group from Banu Makhzum to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who was with Maymuna, and said: "O Messenger of Allah! Abu 'Amr divorced Fatima three times; does she have any maintenance?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: «She has no maintenance.» Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent to her: "Move to the house of Umm Sharik." And he sent to her: "Do not outrun me with yourself." Then he sent to her that Umm Sharik is visited by the first emigrants, so move to Ibn Maktum, for when you take off your head-cover he will not see you. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) married her to Usama ibn Zayd.» End.

Al-Nasir said in *al-Intisaf*: It is not hidden from one who reflects on these verses that the irrevocably divorced woman who is not pregnant has no maintenance, because the verses were brought to explain the obligation. So He obligated residence for every woman in waiting whose mention preceded, and did not obligate anything else. Then He excepted the pregnant women and singled them out by obligating maintenance for them until they give birth, and after this explanation there is no further explanation. And to say after this that maintenance is obligatory for every irrevocably divorced woman in waiting, whether pregnant or not, clearly contradicts the structure of the verse.

Al-Zamakhshari supported the school of Abu Hanifa, saying: The benefit of singling out pregnant women in the mention is that pregnancy may last a long time, so someone might suppose that maintenance is not obligatory because of its length. So they were singled out in the mention to draw attention to cutting off this misconception. The purpose of al-Zamakhshari in this is that the specification should be understood as this benefit, so that it would not have an implication of dropping maintenance for non-pregnant women; because Abu Hanifa equates all of them in the obligation of maintenance. End.

In *al-Iklil*: In the verse is the obligation to spend on the pregnant irrevocably divorced woman until her waiting period ends. Its implication is that the non-pregnant one has no maintenance. And whoever made it obligatory for the pregnant widow used the generality of the verse as evidence. End.

﴿And if they nurse for you﴾: meaning your irrevocably divorced wives from you. ﴿Then give them their payment﴾: that is, for their nursing. ﴿And confer among yourselves in kindness﴾: that is, so that each of you accepts from the other what is commanded of kindness, meaning courtesy and forbearance in nursing and in the payment. The address is to the fathers and the mothers.

(p-5844) **Note:**

In *al-Iklil*: In it is that if the mother asks to nurse him for the customary wage, it is obligatory on the father to pay it to her, and he has no right to hire another to nurse him instead of her. And in it is evidence that the mother has more right to custody (*hadana*).

Ilkiya said: In it is an indication that the wage is due only upon completion of the work. End.

In His words "in kindness" is a demand that the father not haggle and that the mother not be obstinate, because the child is theirs together, and they are partners in it, and in the obligation of compassion toward them. (This was said by al-Zamakhshari.)

﴿But if you disagree﴾: that is, if one of you constrains the other by stubbornness over the payment, or by demanding more and the like, ﴿then another woman will nurse for him﴾. Ibn Jarir said: that is, he has no authority over her, and it is not permitted for him to compel her to nurse him, but he hires a wet-nurse for the child other than his mother who is irrevocably divorced from him.

Al-Zamakhshari said: that is, another will be found, and a nursing woman other than the mother will not be lacking to nurse him. In this there is a touch of rebuke to the mother for obstinacy, as you say to one whom you ask for a need and he delays: "Someone else will do it." You mean: it will not remain undone, and you will be blamed. End.

Al-Nasir said: He singled out the mother for rebuke because what is given on her part is her milk to her child, which is not considered wealth nor is it customarily withheld, especially from a mother to her child; whereas what is given by the father is wealth, which is customarily withheld. So the mother is more deserving of blame and more worthy of reproach. End.

In it there is also an indication of rebuke to the father as well, as one of them verified, because the father, when he was removed from the level of direct address and it was made clear that his obstinacy would not avail, since another nurse is necessary for pay, and she is more compassionate than him, he became in the position of one being rebuked, as mentioned in the answer. And with this is removed what might be said: that obstinacy is the act of both the father and the mother, so why single out the mother by mention in the consequence? Its sum is that both are mentioned in it, but the mother is stated explicitly and the father is alluded to. Ibn Jarir's exposition also points to this.

(p-5845) **Note:**

In *al-Iklil*: It indicates that the mother is not compelled to nurse where another is available and the child accepts her breast; otherwise she is compelled to do so.

Ibn al-'Arabi said: The verse is a basis for the obligation of a child's maintenance upon the father, contrary to those who made it obligatory upon both of them together.

The discussion on the interpretation (ta'wil) of His saying, exalted is He:

[7] ﴿Let the one of wealth spend from his wealth, and whoever has his provision restricted for him, let him spend from what God has given him. God does not burden any soul beyond what He has given it. God will bring about ease after hardship.﴾

﴿Let the one of wealth spend from his wealth﴾ means: from the abundance of his wealth and his riches, upon his divorced wife for the wages of nursing his child by her, and upon his young child. ﴿And whoever has his provision restricted for him﴾ means: whose provision is constricted. ﴿let him spend from what God has given him﴾ means: according to the measure of his wealth and his capacity. ﴿God does not burden any soul beyond what He has given it﴾ means: beyond its capacity and its ability. So He does not burden the poor man with the maintenance of the rich man, nor anyone beyond the obligation that is incumbent upon him. ﴿God will bring about ease after hardship﴾ means: He will grant the one of little means relief after constriction, and richness after poverty, as consolation for the straitened among the poor husbands, a comfort for their divorced wives, a soothing of the hearts of all, and a general glad tidings.

Note:

In al-Iklil: In this verse is the indication that maintenance is assessed according to the condition of the one who spends, in wealth and in poverty, and that the maintenance of the straitened is less than the maintenance of the affluent, not according to the condition of the one who is maintained. Whoever says that there is no annulment of the marriage due to inability to provide maintenance for the wife has taken as evidence His saying: ﴿God does not burden any soul beyond what He has given it.﴾ The verse also recommends that a person consider his own circumstances in maintenance and charity. In a hadith: "Indeed the believer has taken from God a good discipline: when He widens provision for him, he widens, and when He restricts it for him, he restricts."

(p-5846) Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) narrated that Umar ibn al-Khattab asked about Abu Ubayda, and it was said to him: "He wears coarse garments and eats the roughest food." So he sent him a thousand dinars and said to the messenger: "Watch what he does when he takes them." He did not delay before he put on the softest garments and ate the finest food. The messenger came and informed him, and he said, may God have mercy on him: "He interpreted this verse: ﴿Let the one of wealth spend from his wealth, and whoever has his provision restricted for him, let him spend from what God has given him.﴾"

Then God, exalted is He, warned against disobeying Him and transgressing His limits in what He has legislated, out of concern for the rulings that have passed, by His saying, glorified is He:

Commentary on the interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:

[8–9] ﴿And how many a town rebelled against the command of its Lord and His messengers, so We called it to a severe account and punished it with a terrible punishment. So it tasted the evil consequence of its affair, and the outcome of its affair was loss.﴾ [al-Talaq: 8–9]

﴿And how many a town rebelled against the command of its Lord﴾ — i.e., it turned away from it out of arrogance and obstinate opposition. ﴿and His messengers﴾ — i.e., and it likewise turned away from the commands of His messengers. ﴿So We called it to a severe account﴾ — i.e., for what it had put forward, and We left it nothing of it. ﴿And We punished it with a terrible punishment﴾ — i.e., a munkar (disapproved, dreadful) punishment.

﴿So it tasted the evil consequence of its affair﴾ [al-Talaq: 9] — i.e., the consequence of what it had earned and its recompense. ﴿and the outcome of its affair was loss﴾ [al-Talaq: 9] — Ibn Jarir said: i.e., ghabn (a losing bargain), because they sold the bliss of the Hereafter for a base, small worldly gain, and preferred following their desires over following the command of Allah.

Commentary on the interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:

[8–9] ﴿And how many a town rebelled against the command of its Lord and His messengers, so We called it to a severe account and punished it with a terrible punishment. So it tasted the evil consequence of its affair, and the outcome of its affair was loss.﴾ [al-Talaq: 8–9]

﴿And how many a town rebelled against the command of its Lord﴾ — i.e., it turned away from it out of arrogance and obstinate opposition. ﴿and His messengers﴾ — i.e., and it likewise turned away from the commands of His messengers. ﴿So We called it to a severe account﴾ — i.e., for what it had put forward, and We left it nothing of it. ﴿And We punished it with a terrible punishment﴾ — i.e., a munkar (disapproved, dreadful) punishment.

﴿So it tasted the evil consequence of its affair﴾ [al-Talaq: 9] — i.e., the consequence of what it had earned and its recompense. ﴿and the outcome of its affair was loss﴾ [al-Talaq: 9] — Ibn Jarir said: i.e., ghabn (a losing bargain), because they sold the bliss of the Hereafter for a base, small worldly gain, and preferred following their desires over following the command of Allah.

The discussion of His saying, exalted is He:

[10] ﴿Allah has prepared for them a severe punishment. So fear Allah, O people of understanding, who have believed. Allah has indeed sent down to you a reminder.﴾

﴿Allah has prepared for them a severe punishment﴾ means the punishment of the Fire prepared for the Day of Resurrection. ﴿So fear Allah﴾ i.e., fear Him and beware of His seizing by performing His obligations and avoiding His prohibitions. ﴿O people of understanding﴾ i.e., of intellects (ʿuqūl). ﴿who have believed﴾ i.e., who affirmed Allah and His messengers. It is a qualifying adjective (naʿt) for the vocative, or an explicative apposition (ʿaṭf bayān) to it. ﴿Allah has indeed sent down to you a reminder﴾

On the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[11] ﴿A Messenger reciting to you the clear signs of Allah, that He may bring those who believe and do righteous deeds from darkness into light. And whoever believes in Allah and does righteous deeds — He will admit him into gardens beneath which rivers flow, to abide therein forever. Allah has certainly perfected for him a provision.﴾

It means Muhammad (ﷺ). He made him the very reminder (al-dhikr) for emphasis, and therefore ﴿reciting to you﴾ is put in apposition to it. ﴿The clear signs of Allah﴾ means: clear to whoever hears them and reflects upon them, that they are the truth from Allah. ﴿That He may bring those who believe and do righteous deeds from darkness into light﴾ means: from misguidance to guidance. ﴿And whoever believes in Allah and does righteous deeds — He will admit him into gardens beneath which rivers flow, to abide therein forever. Allah has certainly perfected for him a provision﴾ means: He has made it good (ṭayyib). In this there is an expression of wonder at it and of its magnitude.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 65, verse 12:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[12] ﴿It is Allah who created seven heavens and of the earth the like thereof. The command descends among them that you may know that Allah is over all things competent and that Allah has encompassed all things in knowledge.﴾

(p-5848) ﴿It is Allah who created seven heavens and of the earth the like thereof﴾ That is: the One worthy of worship, whose creation this is, not that which is associated with Him. Here are some subtleties:

The first: al-Zamakhshari said: It has been said that there is no verse in the Qur'an that indicates the earths are seven except this one. End quote.

Some astronomers said: As for the earths being seven like the heavens, this is a matter we do not know and do not understand unless it is meant that the earth has seven layers. He said: The truth is to say that the earths being seven, as it appears to us, is one of the illusions of the ancients, and for this reason the word "earth" did not occur in the noble Qur'an in the plural, that is "earths," and it did not occur in it at all that the earths are seven, although it mentioned that the heavens are seven, many times, and each time it mentions the earth alongside them in the singular. Yes! There occurred in it the saying of the Exalted:

﴿It is Allah who created seven heavens and of the earth the like thereof﴾, and it is the only verse from which they understood that the earths are seven. And it, as is not hidden, does not indicate that at all.

He said: For us there are two interpretations of it:

Either the "min" in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and of the earth﴾ is extra (zaa'ida), or it is not extra.

As for the first case: the construction of the verse is thus: Allah is He who created seven heavens and the earth He created the like of them. According to this explanation, this verse indicates that the earth was created like the rest of the wandering planets in every respect. That is: it is one of the planets, and this is a matter that was not known at the time of the Prophet (ﷺ), and no one among the Arabs conceived of it, and that is among the proofs of the truthfulness of the Qur'an. The earth is like the other planets in its substance, in the manner of its creation, in its orbiting around the sun and drawing its light and heat from it, in being inhabited by living beings like the other planets, and in being spherical in shape. The planets, or the heavens, are alike in all respects, and all are created from one substance, (p-5849) namely the substance of the sun, and in one manner, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Have not those who disbelieved seen that the heavens and the earth were a joined mass﴾ [al-Anbiya': 30], that is, one thing, ﴿then We separated them﴾ [al-Anbiya': 30], that is, We separated some of them from others. So the earth was created by Allah exactly like the heavens.

As for the second case: that "min" is not extra, the construction of the verse is thus: Allah is He who created seven heavens and created from the earth an earth like them. So the verse is in the manner of abstraction (tajrid), like your saying: "I have taken seven friends for myself, and from so-and-so I have a friend like them," that is, like them in friendship. Or the construction is: and part of the earth is like them in its matter and its elements. And accordingly, there is in the noble Qur'an not the least evidence that the earths are seven as they claim. End quote.

The second: Ibn al-Athir mentioned in "al-Mathal al-Sa'ir" in the sixth type, on the variation of forms of words, their agreement, and their differing in beauty, in it what is its example:

In this regard is what occurs in use of words in the singular and does not occur in the plural, such as the word "earth," for it occurs in the Qur'an only in the singular. When the heavens are mentioned in the plural, it is brought in the singular alongside them in every place in the Qur'an. And when it was intended to bring it in the plural, it was said: ﴿and of the earth the like thereof﴾ in His saying: ﴿It is Allah who created seven heavens and of the earth the like thereof﴾. End quote.

The third: It was read: "mithlahunna" with the accusative, as a conjunction with "seven," and with the nominative, as a subject (mubtada'), its predicate being "of the earth."

﴿The command descends among them﴾ That is: the command and judgment of Allah proceeds among them, and His dominion takes effect within them. And His saying:

﴿that you may know that Allah is over all things competent and that Allah has encompassed all things in knowledge﴾ is a cause (illah) for "created" and for "descends," or for an implied element that encompasses both, like: he did what he did so that you may know... etc. For each of them indicates the perfection of His power and His knowledge.

(p-5850) Ibn Jarir said: That is: so fear, O people who oppose the command of your Lord, His punishment, for no preventer prevents Him from punishing you. He is competent over that, and He also encompasses your deeds, so nothing of them is hidden from Him. And He counts them against you, so that He may recompense you for them on the day when every soul will be repaid for what it earned.
